title: Symplectic Constraints in Classical Reaction Dynamics: From Gromov's Camel to Reaction Rates
summary: We investigate whether ideas from symplectic topology, in particular Gromov's non-squeezing theorem and symplectic capacity, can provide useful geometric insight into classical reaction dynamics near an index-1 saddle. Using Poincaré-Birkhoff normal form theory, we describe the phase-space structures that organize transport through the transition-state region, including dividing surfaces, normally hyperbolic invariant manifolds (NHIMs), and the associated bath-action geometry.
